# Sentry MCP Server

Connects AI assistants to Sentry for searching errors, analyzing performance, triaging issues, reading documentation, and managing projects — all via the Model Context Protocol.

All connections use OAuth. The first connection will trigger an authentication flow to connect to your Sentry account.

## Connecting

The base MCP server address is: `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp`

You can optionally scope the connection to an organization or project:

  * `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/{organizationSlug}` — scoped to one organization
  * `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/{organizationSlug}/{projectSlug}` — scoped to one project

When scoped, tools automatically default to the constrained org/project and unnecessary discovery tools are hidden. Scoping to a project is recommended when possible.

### Query Parameters

  * `?experimental=1` — Enable forward-looking tool variants and experimental features

Parameters can be combined: `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/my-org/my-project?experimental=1`

## Setup Instructions

### Claude Code
    
    `claude mcp add --transport http sentry https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/{organizationSlug}/{projectSlug}`

### Cursor

Use the "Install MCP Server" button, or manually add to MCP settings:
    
    `{
      "mcpServers": {
        "sentry": {
          "url": "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/{organizationSlug}/{projectSlug}"
        }
      }
    }`

### VSCode

Command Palette → "MCP: Add Server" → HTTP → enter the endpoint:
    
    `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/{organizationSlug}/{projectSlug}`

### Other Clients

Any MCP-compatible client can connect using the HTTP transport at the endpoint URL above.

## Local Server via the Sentry CLI

Install the Sentry CLI and log in, then register `sentry mcp` as a stdio MCP server. It uses the CLI login, so the MCP config needs no token.
    
    `curl https://cli.sentry.dev/install -fsS | bash
    sentry auth login
    claude mcp add sentry -- sentry mcp`

Other clients take the same command:
    
    `{
      "mcpServers": {
        "sentry": {
          "command": "sentry",
          "args": ["mcp"]
        }
      }
    }`

The CLI also installs with `brew install getsentry/tools/sentry`, `npm install -g sentry`, or `irm https://cli.sentry.dev/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows. See https://cli.sentry.dev/getting-started/.

Pass a target after the command to limit it:

  * `sentry mcp my-org/` — Limit to one organization
  * `sentry mcp my-org/my-project` — Limit to a specific project

For self-hosted Sentry, log in with `sentry auth login --url https://sentry.example.com`, then set `SENTRY_HOST` in the MCP server's environment. See https://cli.sentry.dev/self-hosted/.

Run `sentry mcp --help` for every flag and environment variable. To run the server without installing the CLI, use the legacy `npx @sentry/mcp-server` package.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Sentry MCP: Intentional vs. unintentional drops, better field choices, and faster project-scoped requests

October 27, 2026·2 min read

Copy page

Your agent can now tell drops you configured apart from data you're losing, find the right attribute in projects with many fields, and spend less time verifying project-scoped connections.

These updates reached the hosted Sentry MCP server at mcp.sentry.dev on October 21 and 22, 2026.

## Intentional vs. unintentional drops

Each `find_dropped_events` bucket now has a `tags` list. `intentional` marks drops caused by your own configuration, such as sampling, inbound filters, or `before_send`. `unintentional` marks drops you didn't ask for, such as quota, abuse, or invalid data. By Saraj Singh Manes in #1560.

## Better field choices in search

When `search_traces`, `search_logs`, or `search_metrics` write a query from your plain-language request, they now see Sentry's description of each attribute and can page past the first 50 fields. Custom attributes that used to be cut off are reachable, and fields are chosen by what they mean, not just by name. By Nikki Kapadia in #1505 and #1518.

## Faster project-scoped connections

If your connection is scoped to a single project, the project check that runs before requests now fetches less data. If that check times out, the server skips it for 60 seconds instead of making each request wait up to five seconds again. By Miguel Betegón in #1551.

## Fixes

  * Search tools no longer fail when a time series returns text values, such as `max(timestamp)` or `latest_event()`. Text series keep their exact values and skip peak and total summaries. With Miguel Betegón in #1424.
  * `create_project` with a `repository` no longer fails when the organization has repositories that aren't linked to an external provider (#1297).
  * Actions taken through Claude's hosted apps now show up in issue activity as Claude instead of Claude Desktop (#1516).

## Are you using the stdio MCP server?

There was no new `@sentry/mcp-server` release in this period. The latest version is still 0.42.0, so these changes are only on mcp.sentry.dev until the next npm release.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Systeme.io MCP, answered.

Do I need a separate server per app?

No. That is the point of it. One Activepieces server exposes Systeme.io alongside every other piece you connect, so your client keeps a single connection.

Is the Systeme.io MCP server free?

Yes. Activepieces is open source and free to start, and the MCP server is included on every plan, from the free cloud tier to any self-hosted deployment.

# Sentry MCP

The Sentry MCP Server brings Sentry’s full issue context into systems that support the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Connect through Cequence AI Gateway to access Sentry issues and errors, search for errors in specific files, query projects and organizations, manage DSNs, and invoke Seer for automated analysis and fix suggestions—all from your AI client.

## Overview​

Sentry MCP is a remote, vendor-hosted MCP server provided by Sentry. You connect to it from Cequence AI Gateway; Sentry hosts and manages the server so you always get the latest functionality.

  * Server URL: `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp`
  * Transport: HTTP (Streamable HTTP with automatic SSE fallback)
  * Hosted by: Sentry

The server is production-ready; MCP as a technology is still evolving, so changes may occur. Feedback and issues can be reported on GitHub.

## Supported authentication types​

Type  | Supported  | Notes
--- | --- | ---
OAuth 2.1  | Yes  | Recommended. Uses Dynamic Client Registration (DCR).   8. Complete the setup as prompted, select tools, and deploy.

Use the generated MCP server URL in your client as described in the Client Configuration docs. For detailed UI steps and screenshots, see Create a third-party MCP Server.

## Additional information​

  * Seer integration: MCP and Seer are complementary—MCP brings Sentry context into your LLM; Seer is used for deep issue analysis and automated debugging. You can use MCP to invoke Seer for complex workflows.
  * Verified clients: Sentry MCP has been verified with Claude (Desktop and Claude.ai), Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Factory Droid, Amp, VS Code/GitHub Copilot, Vercel v0, Warp, Windsurf, and other clients that support OAuth and remote MCP.
  * Troubleshooting: If OAuth fails, try the legacy Remote MCP configuration; ensure the URL is `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp` (or `https://mcp.sentry.dev/sse` for SSE). Clear cached auth if needed (for example `~/.mcp-auth`).
  * Official documentation: Sentry MCP Server, Live demo, GitHub.

# Sentry

Connect Sentry so users can search errors, triage issues, and inspect their permitted Sentry projects through Sentry's hosted MCP server.

Use a Sentry account on sentry.io with access to the organizations and projects your users need. You create nothing in Sentry before adding the server. Each person signs in to Sentry in their browser the first time they use the server, after you connect your credentials.

### Add the server in Speakeasy

  1. In the Speakeasy AI Control Plane sidebar, under MCP Gateway, select MCP.
  2. Select Add new to open Add MCP server.

If a Sentry catalog entry for `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp` is listed:

  1. Choose From the catalog.
  2. On the MCP Catalog page, enter `Sentry` in Search MCP servers….
  3. Open the Sentry entry.
  4. Select Add.
  5. In the Add to Project dialog, under Identity, keep User Identity selected.
  6. Select Add to Project. If the dialog offers a Guardrails step, select Skip for now.
  7. Open the created Sentry server from the result.

If it is not listed, use the custom remote path:

  1. Choose Hosted remotely.

  2. On New remote MCP server, paste this value into MCP server URL:
    
    `
    
    https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp
    
    `

  3. Select Verify connectivity.

  4. Under Identity, keep User Identity selected.

  5. Select Save. This opens the server’s Overview page.

When it adds the server, Speakeasy discovers Sentry’s identity provider and registers a client automatically. There is no Client ID or secret to paste. If that cannot complete, the server is kept Disabled and the result says to finish setup in Settings > Identity; on the catalog path it reads “Added, but disabled until identity is set up.” with Finish setup.

### Connect your credentials

Open the server’s Settings and find the Identity section. It normally shows User Identity with the `https://mcp.sentry.dev` provider and Auto-Configure already set; skip to step 5.

  1. Select User Identity.
  2. Confirm the preselected provider is `https://mcp.sentry.dev`. A provider that does not exist yet shows Will be created. If a different provider is selected, open the picker, search for `mcp.sentry.dev` in Search authorization servers…, and choose it.
  3. Keep Auto-Configure selected.
  4. Select Save.
  5. If the server shows Disabled, open Settings > Danger Zone > Server Availability and turn on Enable MCP server so it shows Enabled.

The first time each person uses the server, they approve Sentry’s MCP consent screen, sign in to Sentry, and authorize access. They can only reach what their Sentry account already can.

This guide covers setup only. For anything beyond it — billing, tool behavior, limits — see Sentry’s MCP documentation.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We’ll unpack this more later in the post, but jumping ahead - yes, as the title of this post suggests - Sentry has an MCP server. You can learn more about it by visiting the MCP server address directly, or in our product docs.

The Sentry MCP has support for all the newest fun bells and whistles, including: 

  * Remote hosted (preferred) or local STDIO mode (we strongly recommend the hosted version. It’s lower friction and you’ll always have the latest functionality/stability)
  * OAuth supportto enable logging in via your existing Sentry organization, so you’ll have clear access to your organization and projects
  * Streamable HTTP with graceful fallback to SSE if your client doesn’t support it
  * 16 different tool calls, including prompts, to support bringing wide context in from Sentry, including tools like project information, issues, finding or creating projects and DSNs, and even calling our AI agent Seer to generate root causes and fix issues (see the full list here)

The Sentry MCP can be added to most providers that support OAuth by adding the following content to your MCP Configuration file: 
    
    `{
     "mcpServers": {
       "Sentry": {
         "url": "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp"
       }
     }
    }`

For clients that don’t support OAuth, you can continue to use the existing Remote MCP endpoint configuration. If your client doesn’t support Streamable HTTP yet, this will automatically fallback to the SSE connection.  
    
    `{
      "mcpServers": {
        "sentry": {
          "command": "npx",
          "args": [
            "-y",
            "mcp-remote@latest",
            "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp"
          ]
        }
      }
    }`
